Short notes on the methods the [proposal](../phd/index.qmd) uses, each explained, implemented and tested
on real market data. The list is deliberately short: it covers what the research needs rather than
everything that could be covered.

| Area | Note | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| Forecasting models | [Logistic regression](logistic-regression/index.qmd) | Interpretable baseline forecaster (02) |
| | [Gradient boosting (XGBoost)](xgboost/index.qmd) | Nonlinear benchmark model (02) |
| | [Long short-term memory (LSTM)](lstms/index.qmd) | Compact deep-learning forecaster (02) |
| | [Ensemble methods and model combination](ensemble-methods/index.qmd) | Fixed and adaptive numerical ensembles, the benchmark LLM decisions must beat (02, 10) |
| Regimes | [Markov-switching regression](markov-switching-regression/index.qmd) | Optional regime probabilities (02, 08) |
| Evaluation | [Probability calibration and conformal prediction](probability-calibration/index.qmd) | Calibrated probabilities and Brier scores (02, 10) |
| | [Walk-forward validation](walk-forward-validation/index.qmd) | Testing only on unseen data (10) |
| | [Avoiding data leakage](data-leakage/index.qmd) | Point-in-time data and purged boundaries (01, 10) |
| LLMs in decisions | [LLMs versus conventional ML](../ai-systems/llms-vs-conventional-ml/index.qmd) | What language models add, and where numerical models are better (04) |
| | [Hallucination risk when LLMs meet financial data](../ai-systems/hallucination-risk/index.qmd) | Why the semantic layer and claim checks exist (03) |
| | [Why an LLM must never directly place trades](../ai-systems/why-llms-never-trade/index.qmd) | Why deterministic controls have the final say (05) |

: Numbers refer to components of the [system architecture](../phd/architecture.html). {.striped}
